To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the feedback-related negativity (a brain potential) is modulated by the probability that feedback is positive or negative in observational learning, and (ii) that the modulation of this brain potential is similar in observational and active learning.
the feedback-related negativity ( FRN) is modulated by the probability of feedback in observational learning.
the FRN, a component related to the anterior cingulated cortex (ACC) and reflecting feedback processing, is modulated by the feedback probability in observational feedback learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural correlates of observational learning.
the question of how people learn from other people.
the neural correlates of observational learning and their relation to the learning process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FRN is not only a marker of the reward system but also reflects the general cognitive processing of feedback.
the FRN is modulated by outcome probability in active as well as in observational feedback-based learning.
feedback processing in observational learning is modulated by the expectancy of feedback, but the exact mechanisms of the underlying brain processes are still not clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that FRN amplitude is reduced when feedback probability is high, but that the reduction in FRN amplitude is stronger for negative than positive feedback when feedback probability is low.
the feedback-related negativity is a reliable marker of feedback processing, but its modulation by feedback expectancy depends on the task setting.
the ACC is involved in feedback processing during observational learning and the FRN is sensitive to outcome expectancy in this setting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
feedback expectancy modulations of the FRN and P3 are present in observational learning.
the FRN and P3 are modulated by the feedback probability, but the FRN is modulated by valence only for very low feedback probability.
the FRN is modulated by the probability of feedback in observational learning.
